items.markingKey: (a) The Clemmensen reduction: the reduction of a carbonyl group to CH₂ with zinc amalgam and concentrated HCl.
options: the Clemmensen reduction
the aldol condensation
the Wolff–Kishner reduction
Tollens' reagent

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Iron scrap and HCl are preferred for reducing nitrobenzene to aniline.
Reason (R): FeCl₂ formed is hydrolysed, releasing HCl during the reaction.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) So only a small amount of acid is needed.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

Reason (R): In a galvanic cell oxidation takes place at the anode.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) > E°(Zn²⁺/Zn), so copper cannot reduce Zn²⁺. R is a true statement.

items.stem: Give two differences between RNA and DNA.
items.answer: RNA: sugar is ribose; bases A, G, C and U. DNA: double-stranded helix; can replicate and carries hereditary information.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. RNA – sugar is ribose; bases A, G, C and U; DNA – double-stranded helix; can replicate and carries hereditary information.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Molality depends on temperature.”
items.answer: Molality depends only on masses, so it is independent of temperature.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Molality depends only on masses, so it is independent of temperature.

items.stem: Give two differences between methanol and glycerol (propane-1,2,3-triol).
items.answer: Methanol: highly poisonous, can cause blindness; used as a solvent and to make methanal. Glycerol (propane-1,2,3-triol): has three –OH groups; used in cosmetics and to make nitroglycerine.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. methanol – highly poisonous, can cause blindness; used as a solvent and to make methanal; glycerol (propane-1,2,3-triol) – has three –OH groups; used in cosmetics and to make nitroglycerine.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as biologically important coordination compound or industrial or analytical use of complexes: chlorophyll (Mg), extraction of gold with cyanide, estimation of hardness of water with EDTA, Wilkinson's catalyst for hydrogenation.
items.answer: chlorophyll (Mg) – biologically important coordination compound; extraction of gold with cyanide – industrial or analytical use of complexes; estimation of hardness of water with EDTA – industrial or analytical use of complexes; Wilkinson's catalyst for hydrogenation – industrial or analytical use of complexes.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as reaction of moderate rate or very fast reaction: inversion of cane sugar, precipitation of AgCl on mixing AgNO₃ and NaCl, decomposition of H₂O₂ without catalyst, neutralisation of HCl by NaOH.
items.answer: inversion of cane sugar – reaction of moderate rate; precipitation of AgCl on mixing AgNO₃ and NaCl – very fast reaction; decomposition of H₂O₂ without catalyst – reaction of moderate rate; neutralisation of HCl by NaOH – very fast reaction.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Friedel–Crafts acylation of benzene gives benzaldehyde.”
items.answer: With CH₃COCl/AlCl₃ it gives acetophenone; benzaldehyde comes from Gatterman–Koch or Etard reaction.

A current of 1 A is passed through a solution of NiSO₄ for 20 minutes. Calculate the mass of Ni deposited at the cathode. (Molar mass of Ni = 58.7 g mol⁻¹, F = 96500 C mol⁻¹)

items.answer: Sc³⁺ < Cr³⁺ < Mn²⁺

items.stem: Pure (+)-lactic acid has a specific rotation of +3.8°. A sample of it prepared by Sneha shows a specific rotation of +0.760°. Calculate the optical purity (enantiomeric excess) and the percentage of each enantiomer.
items.markingKey: Optical purity = observed/pure × 100 = 0.760/3.8 × 100 = 20% (1); (+) = 50 + ee/2 = 60%, (−) = 40% (the rest is racemic) (2).

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct order of levels of protein structure: secondary, quaternary, tertiary. Give a reason.
items.answer: secondary → tertiary → quaternary
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order secondary → tertiary → quaternary; 1 mark for the reason: Sequence → local folding (α-helix/β-sheet) → overall folding → association of subunits.

items.stem: Give two differences between a solution with negative deviation and a solution with positive deviation.
items.answer: A solution with negative deviation: ΔmixV negative (volume decreases); forms maximum boiling azeotrope at a certain composition. A solution with positive deviation: ΔmixV positive (volume increases); A–B interactions weaker than A–A and B–B.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. a solution with negative deviation – ΔmixV negative (volume decreases); forms maximum boiling azeotrope at a certain composition; a solution with positive deviation – ΔmixV positive (volume increases); A–B interactions weaker than A–A and B–B.

items.stem:
An important alcohol has these features: highly poisonous, can cause blindness; made from CO and H₂ at 573–673 K over ZnO–Cr₂O₃; used as a solvent and to make methanal.
(i) Identify the alcohol. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were glycerol (propane-1,2,3-triol)? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Methanol (ii) called wood spirit (iii) has three –OH groups; by-product of soap manufacture

items.stem:
A coordination compound has the following role: contains platinum(II); square planar cis isomer; anticancer drug.
(i) Identify the compound. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were haemoglobin? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Cisplatin (ii) formula [PtCl₂(NH₃)₂] (iii) carries oxygen; metal is held in a porphyrin ring
items.markingKey: (i) cisplatin – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: formula [PtCl₂(NH₃)₂] – 1 mark. (iii) for haemoglobin: contains iron; red pigment of blood; carries oxygen – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between second order and zero order on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A reaction shows the following behaviour: shown by the decomposition of NH₃ on hot platinum at high pressure. What is the order of the reaction – second order or zero order? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Second order: a plot of 1/[R] against t is a straight line; half-life is inversely proportional to initial concentration; units of k are mol⁻¹ L s⁻¹. Zero order: a plot of [R] against t is a straight line with slope −k; half-life is directly proportional to initial concentration; units of k are mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹. (b) Zero order.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: zero order; 1 mark: “shown by the decomposition of NH₃ on hot platinum at high pressure” is a feature of zero order.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between the mercury cell and the H₂–O₂ fuel cell on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A cell has these features: zinc–mercury amalgam anode. Identify the cell – the mercury cell or the H₂–O₂ fuel cell? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) The mercury cell: zinc–mercury amalgam anode; paste of HgO and carbon as cathode; paste of KOH and ZnO as electrolyte. The H₂–O₂ fuel cell: H₂ and O₂ bubbled through porous carbon electrodes into concentrated NaOH; used in the Apollo space programme; product water can be used for drinking. (b) The mercury cell.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: the mercury cell; 1 mark: “zinc–mercury amalgam anode” is a feature of the mercury cell.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between potassium manganate (K₂MnO₄) and potassium permanganate (KMnO₄) on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) An oxidising agent has these properties: paramagnetic with one unpaired electron. Identify the compound – potassium manganate (K₂MnO₄) or potassium permanganate (KMnO₄)? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Potassium manganate (K₂MnO₄): green compound; Mn in the +6 state; disproportionates in acid to MnO₄⁻ and MnO₂. Potassium permanganate (KMnO₄): dark purple crystals; made from pyrolusite via green K₂MnO₄; in acid gains 5 electrons to give Mn²⁺. (b) Potassium manganate (K₂MnO₄).
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: potassium manganate (K₂MnO₄); 1 mark: “paramagnetic with one unpaired electron” is a feature of potassium manganate (K₂MnO₄).
